recent_posts.title: NHK World's Texico teaches programming concepts to kids without a computer
recent_posts.summary: NHK World's Texico program teaches core programming concepts to children without using a computer. Using physical props like toy trains and playing cards, the ten-episode series (available in English and French) covers ideas such as analysis, abstraction, simulation, and algorithms. Real-world examples like mail sorting and fireworks packing illustrate algorithmic thinking in everyday contexts.

recent_posts.title: FPGA board runs 10240 oscillators for hardware Fourier audio synthesis
recent_posts.summary: A hardware project cramming 10,240 individually controllable oscillators onto a Terasic DE10-nano FPGA board. Rather than traditional voice-based polyphony, the creator built a 'spectrum engine' that implements Fourier synthesis directly in hardware — each oscillator has independently controllable frequency, phase, and amplitude. This massively parallel approach enables real-time audio synthesis without software overhead, capable of emulating various synthesis techniques and demonstrated as an 80-voice polyphonic synthesizer.

recent_posts.title: Google silently installed a 4GB LLM in Chrome and users didn't consent
recent_posts.summary: Google has quietly bundled a 4GB Gemini Nano LLM into Chrome without user consent, causing performance slowdowns and disk activity for billions of users. The author argues this sets a troubling precedent where software silently installs resource-hungry AI models users can't control or opt out of. Drawing a parallel to Microsoft's Clippy, the piece calls for local LLMs to be opt-in, user-controlled applications rather than hidden components — and suggests tools like llama.cpp represent a healthier model where users own their AI and their data.

recent_posts.title: A 1947 Radio Gets A Face Lift
recent_posts.summary: A 1947 Arvin 664A AM radio found in a home-built wooden cabinet gets restored to working condition. The restoration involved troubleshooting, replacing all old capacitors, cleaning the cabinet, fitting a new speaker grille, and adding a new tuning dial window. The radio ultimately sounded good after the work was completed.

recent_posts.title: LightInk, A Solar Powered ESP32 Smartwatch
recent_posts.summary: LightInk is a solar-powered smartwatch built around the ESP32-PICO-D4 microcontroller and an e-ink display. The key innovation is a power optimization hack: instead of booting from flash (which takes 28ms and consumes significant energy), the firmware stores everything needed for display updates in the ESP32's RTC memory, enabling microsecond wake times. This cuts boot-related power consumption by roughly two-thirds, making solar charging viable for everyday use. The watch also supports GPS and LoRa, though those features are power-hungry and should be used sparingly.

recent_posts.title: Hamster wheel generator used to charge a smartphone via energy harvesting
recent_posts.summary: A hobbyist project that converts hamster wheel motion into electrical energy to charge a smartphone. The build uses a CJMCU-2557 module with the TI BQ25570 energy harvesting IC, which accepts 0.1–5.1V input and handles the irregular power generation from a hamster's unpredictable running pace. Harvested energy is stored in a supercapacitor and then used to charge salvaged 18650 Li-ion cells, which can provide enough power to begin charging a phone after a night of hamster activity.

recent_posts.title: Teardown Of A Shahed-136 Gimbaled Camera
recent_posts.summary: A teardown of a gimbaled camera recovered from a shot-down Shahed-136 drone in Ukraine reveals that the hardware is almost entirely composed of off-the-shelf components sourced from sites like AliExpress. Key components include an Artix-7 FPGA board, an Hi3519 SoC for camera feed handling, a thermal camera for night operations, and a relay board — all commercial development boards and modules. The gimbal assembly similarly uses mostly Western components, sometimes with lasered-off markings. This continues a pattern seen in previous Shahed-136 teardowns, contrasting with more custom hardware found in Russian missile systems.

recent_posts.title: Sunlight Powered, Sunlight Readable: Solar Case For Nook Simple Touch
recent_posts.summary: A maker received a batch of old Nook Simple Touch e-readers and designed 3D-printed solar-powered cases for them. The build uses a pair of solar panels integrated into the case, connected via a TP4056-based charger wired to the battery test points rather than the 5V supply — avoiding unnecessary WiFi activity during low-power charging. The panels are reportedly capable of trickle-charging the device even under artificial light. The design is open source, with SketchUp files and STL exports available on Thingiverse, and a rooting guide for the Nook is also included.

recent_posts.title: A Shortwave Sensor To Monitor The Ionosphere
recent_posts.summary: A DIY shortwave propagation monitor built by mircemk measures ionosphere conditions by detecting received shortwave signal strength using a CA3089-based circuit. The device amplifies signals in the 1-40 MHz range and outputs a smoothed voltage readable by an Arduino Nano with OLED display, allowing observation of how solar activity and time of day affect ionospheric propagation.

recent_posts.title: TagTinker Lets You Hack Electronic Shelf Labels
recent_posts.summary: TagTinker is a Flipper Zero application for hacking infrared electronic shelf labels (ESLs). Built on prior protocol research by furrtek, it lets users scan NFC tags on ESLs to identify them, push custom bitmap images, or run live dashboards using a Flipper WiFi devboard. The tool lowers the barrier to experimenting with e-paper shelf tags significantly.
